items.title: Consciousness and Name-and-Form, Bundled Like Two Reeds

items.zh: 又此異熟識即依名色而轉，由必依託六依轉故，是故經言名色緣識。俱有依根曰色，等無間滅依根曰名，隨其所應為六識所依。依止彼故，乃至命終諸識流轉。又五色根、若根所依大種、若根處所、若彼能生大種曰色。所餘曰名。由識執受諸根，墮相續法方得流轉；故此二種依止於識相續不斷。由此道理，於現在世，識緣名色，名色緣識，猶如束蘆，乃至命終相依而轉。如是名為從前際，中際諸行緣起生；中際生已，流轉不絕。
items.en: Further, this ripening consciousness operates only in dependence on name-and-form, since it must operate resting on the six sense-bases — this is why the sūtras say name-and-form conditions consciousness. And because consciousness grasps and sustains the sense-faculties, they fall into the pattern of a continuing process and are thereby able to transmigrate — so these two, in turn, depend on consciousness to continue unbroken. By this same reasoning, in the present life, consciousness conditions name-and-form and name-and-form conditions consciousness, exactly like two bundled reeds, depending on each other all the way to the end of life. This, then, is what is meant by dependent origination's arising from the past into the present, and by the present, once arisen, continuing to flow on unbroken.

items.zh: 當知此中依胎生者，說流轉次第。若卵生濕生者，除處母胎，餘如前說。若於有色有情聚中，謂欲、色界受化生者，諸根決定圓滿而生，與前差別。若於無色界，以名為依，及色種子為依，識得生起；以識為依，名及色種子轉。從此種子，色雖斷絕，後更得生；與前差別。
items.en: It should be understood that the sequence of transmigration just given describes those born from the womb. For those born from an egg or from moisture, the whole account applies just the same, apart from the stage of dwelling in a mother's womb. Among embodied beings born by spontaneous transformation — desire-realm and form-realm beings alike — every faculty arises at once, fully complete, unlike the gradual unfolding just described. In the formless realm, consciousness arises resting on name and on the seed of form; and, in turn, name and the seed of form continue resting on consciousness. Though form's actual manifestation is thereby interrupted there, it will arise again later from this same seed — this is how the formless realm differs from the rest.

items.zh: 又由福業，生欲界人天；由非福業，生諸惡趣；由不動業，生色、無色界。云何不生？由不生故，趣清淨究竟。
items.en: Further: by meritorious karma one is born among the humans and gods of the desire realm; by demeritorious karma one is born into the unfortunate destinies; by unmoving karma one is born into the form or formless realm. And what is non-arising? It is by such non-arising that one turns towards the final end of purification.

items.zh: 云何從中際，後際諸行緣起生？

items.title: Two Kinds of Ignorance, and the Projecting Cause That Plants Five Seeds for the Next Life

items.zh: 謂中際已生補特伽羅，受二種先業果。謂受內異熟果，及境界所生受增上果。此補特伽羅或聞非正法故，或先串習故，於二果愚。由愚內異熟果故，於後有生苦不如實知；由迷後有後際無明增上力故，如前於諸行若作若增長。
items.en: A person who has already arisen in the present receives two results from past karma: the inward ripened result, and the dominant result arising from contact with the outward environment. Such a person, whether from hearing teachings that are not the genuine Dharma, or from prior habituation, remains ignorant of both these results. Through ignorance of the inward ripened result, one fails to truly know the suffering of a further existence; and through this same delusion about that further existence — ignorance regarding what is yet to come — one continues, exactly as before, either performing or intensifying karmic formations.

items.zh: 由此新所作業，故說此識名隨業識。即於現法中，說無明為緣故行生，行為緣故識生。此識於現法中名為因識，能攝受後生果識故。又總依一切識說名六識身。又即此識是後有名色種子之所隨逐，此名色種子是後有六處種子之所隨逐，此六處種子是後有觸種子之所隨逐，此種子觸是後有受種子之所隨逐。如是總名於中際中後有引因應知，
items.en: By this newly performed karma, this consciousness is called karma-bound consciousness. It is in this way that, within the present existence, ignorance conditions the arising of formations, and formations condition the arising of consciousness. Within the present existence this consciousness is called cause-consciousness, since it is able to gather in the result-consciousness of a further birth. And this same consciousness is followed by the seed of a further existence's name-and-form; that seed of name-and-form is followed by the seed of the six sense-bases of a further existence; that seed of the six sense-bases is followed by the seed of contact; and that seed of contact is followed by the seed of feeling. All of this, taken together, should be understood as the projecting cause laid down within the present existence for a further existence.

items.zh: 由此能引識乃至受一期身故。

items.title: Craving, Grasping, and Becoming: The Generating Cause That Waters the Seed

items.zh: 由先異熟果愚引後有已，又由第二境界所生受果愚故，起緣境界受愛。由此愛故，或發欲求，或發有求，或執欲取，或執見、戒及我語取。由此愛取和合資潤，令前引因轉名為有。即是後有生因所攝。
items.en: Having already, through ignorance of the inward ripened result, projected a further existence, one is further, through ignorance of the result arising from the outward environment, moved to crave the feeling that contact with that environment produces. Through this craving, one gives rise either to craving for sensory desire or craving for further existence; and one clings either to the grasping of sensory desire, or to the grasping of views, of precepts and vows, or of the doctrine of a self. Through the moistening union of this craving and grasping, the previously projected cause is transformed and named "becoming" — and this, precisely, is what is meant by the generating cause of a further existence.

items.title: From Death to the Next Birth, and Why Grief Belongs at Birth, Not Death

items.zh: 從此無間，命既終已，隨先引因所引識等受最為後，此諸行生，或漸或頓。如是於現法中，無明觸所生受為緣故愛，愛為緣故取，取為緣故有，有為緣故生，生為緣故老病死等諸苦差別。或於生處次第現前，或復種子隨逐應知。
items.en: Immediately following this, once life has ended, the formations belonging to consciousness and the rest of the seeds trailing from the earlier projecting cause arise — either gradually or all at once. And so, within the present existence: feeling arisen from ignorance-tainted contact conditions craving; craving conditions grasping; grasping conditions becoming; becoming conditions birth; and birth conditions the varied sufferings of old age, sickness, and death. These may appear in fixed sequence at the very place of birth, or they may instead remain as trailing seeds still awaiting their occasion — so it should be understood.

items.zh: 如是於中際中，無明緣行等、受緣愛等為因緣故，後際諸行生。
items.en: Thus, within the present existence, it is by ignorance conditioning formations and the rest, and by feeling conditioning craving and the rest, taken together as cause and condition, that the formations of a further existence arise.

items.title: Turning Towards Purification: Hearing the Dharma, and an Arhat's Karma That Even Prison Bars Could Not Undo

items.zh: 復有先集資糧，於現法中，從他聞音，及於二果諸行，若於彼因、彼滅、彼趣滅行如理作意，由此如理作意為緣，正見得生，從此次第得學無學清淨智見。
items.en: There is, further, one who has already gathered the provisions for practice, who in the present existence hears the teaching from another, and who applies sound reasoning attention to the two results just described, to their cause, to their cessation, and to the practice leading to that cessation. By this sound reasoning attention as condition, right view arises; and from this, in due sequence, one attains the purified wisdom and insight of a trainee, and then of one beyond training.

items.title: When Ignorance Ceases, the Whole Chain Ceases: Wisdom-Liberation and Mind-Liberation

items.zh: 由此智見，無明及愛永斷無餘。由此斷故，於彼所緣不如實知無明觸所生受亦復永斷。由此斷故，永離無明，於現法中證慧解脫。若於無明觸所生受相應心中所有貪愛，即於此心得離繫故，貪愛永滅，於現法中證心解脫。
items.en: By this wisdom and insight, ignorance and craving are severed without remainder. By this severing, the feeling arisen from ignorance-tainted contact, which does not know its object as it truly is, is likewise severed forever. By this severing, ignorance is forever left behind, and liberation through wisdom is realised in this very existence. And the craving present in the mind associated with feeling arisen from ignorance-tainted contact, once that mind is released from this bondage, is forever extinguished, and liberation through mind is realised in this very existence.

items.zh: 設彼無明不永斷者，依於識等受最為後所有諸行後際應生；由無明滅故，更不復起，得無生法。是故說言：無明滅故，行滅；次第乃至異熟生觸滅故，異熟生受滅。
items.en: Were that ignorance not forever severed, the formations belonging to consciousness and the rest, down to feeling, would still arise in a further existence; but because ignorance has ceased, they no longer arise at all, and the state of non-arising is attained. This is why it is said: because ignorance ceases, formations cease; and so in sequence, down to: because ripened contact ceases, ripened feeling ceases.

items.zh: 於現法中無明滅故，無明觸滅；無明觸滅故，無明觸所生受滅；無明觸所生受滅故，愛滅；愛滅故，如前得無生法。由此故說取等惱最為後諸行永滅。
items.en: Within the present existence, because ignorance ceases, ignorance-tainted contact ceases; because ignorance-tainted contact ceases, the feeling arisen from it ceases; because that feeling ceases, craving ceases; and because craving ceases, the state of non-arising is attained just as before. This is why it is said that grasping and the rest, down to every remaining formation, are forever extinguished.

blocks.text: Today's reading gives the treatise's account of the twelve links of dependent origination in the forward direction (how saṃsāra continues) and then in reverse (how it ends). The key Yogācāra contribution is the division into **projecting** and **generating** causes, which explains how the twelve links span two or three lives.

Consciousness and name-and-form depend on each other "like two bundled reeds". Venerable Miào Jìng: "Stand one reed up and it won't stand; bind many together and they stand." The ālayavijñāna needs a body to hold; the body lives only while it is held (Day 6).

A person in this life receives two results of past karma: the inner ripened result (one's body and mind) and the dominant result (one's environment). Not understanding these, one acts in ignorance of two kinds. Master Cháng Bǎi: ignorance of ripened results (not knowing that good and evil bear fruit, so one does harm) and ignorance of ultimate truth (not seeing non-self, so even good deeds keep one in saṃsāra).

Through ignorance, one makes karma (**formations**), which perfumes **consciousness** with seeds: the seeds of name-and-form, the six sense-bases, contact, and feeling for a future life. This set is the **projecting cause** (引因). Venerable Miào Jìng: ignorance, formations, and consciousness *project*; the five links from consciousness to feeling are *projected*, present now only as seeds.

At the end of life, **craving** and **grasping** "moisten" the projected seeds (Day 35: "craving is what moistens"), and they are transformed and named **becoming** (有). Becoming is the **generating cause** (生因) of the next existence, which then appears as **birth**, followed by **ageing and death**.

So the twelve links describe two lives with an overlap: one life's ignorance, formations, and consciousness plant seeds; at its end, craving and grasping water them; the next life's birth unfolds what was planted. The five "projected" links are both the seeds now and the experience then.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "Many grieve at death and rejoice at birth; from the Dharma's view, one should weep at birth, since birth ensures ageing, sickness, and death."

The third aspect of the essence of dependent origination is turning towards purification. Right view arises in one who has gathered the provisions, "hears the teaching from another", and attends soundly to the two results, their causes, their cessation, and the path. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is not yet the right view of the eightfold path, but the view gained by hearing and reflection before the path of seeing.

By cultivating this view, ignorance is cut, and "**liberation through wisdom**" (慧解脫) is realised in this very life; craving is extinguished, and "**liberation of mind**" (心解脫) is realised. Venerable Miào Jìng shows where craving begins with a personal example: "I love dumplings; someone mentions dumplings and my mouth waters." Seeing that moment, feeling turning into craving, is where the chain can be cut.

quiz.q: The text says consciousness and name-and-form are "like two bundled reeds." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the simile?
options: one reed won't stand alone, but bundled they stand — ālaya and name-and-form depend on each other
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Stand one reed up and it won't stand; bind many together and they stand." Master Cháng Bǎi: without the ālaya there's no name-and-form, and name-and-form must rest on the ālaya to continue — like a bundle of reeds.

quiz.q: According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what are the two kinds of ignorance that drive karma?
options: ignorance of ripened results — not knowing good and evil bear fruit, so making demerit; and ignorance of ultimate truth
errors of view and of thought
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Ignorance has two kinds: ignorance of ripened results and ignorance of the ultimate." Venerable Miào Jìng: one ignorant of ultimate truth may avoid evil and do good — making merit or unmoving karma — yet remains in saṃsāra.

quiz.q: The text calls the seeds following consciousness "the projecting cause for a further existence." How does Venerable Miào Jìng divide projecting and projected?
options: ignorance-formations-consciousness project; the five from consciousness to feeling are projected
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The earlier 'ignorance conditions formations, formations condition consciousness' is what projects; these five are what's projected." Master Cháng Bǎi: these five are the body of result. Craving, grasping, and becoming generate; birth and ageing-death are generated.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how does the projecting cause come to be called "becoming"?
options: craving and grasping moisten it together, transforming it into becoming — the generating cause of a further existence
quiz.why: "Through the moistening union of this craving and grasping, the previously projected cause is transformed and named" becoming — the generating cause of a further existence. Master Cháng Bǎi: craving and grasping together moisten the seeds, turning the projecting cause into karmic becoming.

quiz.q: The text says birth conditions ageing, sickness, and death. Master Cháng Bǎi notes people grieve at death and rejoice at birth. What does the Dharma say?
options: one should weep at birth, since birth guarantees ageing, sickness, and death
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Many grieve at death and rejoice at birth; from the Dharma's view, one should weep at birth, since birth ensures ageing, sickness, and death." Venerable Miào Jìng: with birth comes infancy, childhood, youth, middle age, old age.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, on what does right view arise?
options: having gathered provisions, hearing from another, and attending soundly to the two results, their cause, cessation, and path — with sound attention as condition
quiz.why: "One who has already gathered the provisions for practice, who in the present existence hears the teaching from another, and who applies sound reasoning attention … By this sound reasoning attention as condition, right view arises." Then come trainee's and adept's insight. Master Cháng Bǎi: sound attention reflects on the four truths, seeing life as truly suffering.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how are liberation through wisdom and liberation through mind each realised?
options: wisdom-liberation by leaving ignorance behind; mind-liberation by the extinction of craving
quiz.why: "By this severing, ignorance is forever left behind, and liberation through wisdom is realised in this very existence"; craving "is forever extinguished, and liberation through mind is realised." Venerable Miào Jìng: once ignorance is cut, the mind meets all things without grasping feeling.
